budget.rationale: The independently itemized $13,350–$19,100 family band can approach the $15,000 preference only near its low case and has a material premium-price tail.

weather.rationale: Mid-June is generally favorable for the Riviera and Provence, but inland heat, exposed coast paths, wind and fire restrictions require early starts and recovery afternoons.

swim.rationale: The plan has repeated sea/lake/pool opportunities and a genuine Antibes sand day, but Nice is pebbles and the historical June Mediterranean planning range is only moderately warm.

variety.rationale: The canonical route explicitly balances coast and swimming, towns and food, Calanques nature, lake/lavender scenery, art and Roman/medieval history.

ease.rationale: Only three bases and one mode change keep the route coherent: five car-free Riviera nights, then one one-way rental through Cassis and Aix to Marseille Airport.

food.rationale: Every base and remote day has named pizza, pasta, burger or plain-food coverage, while markets and apartment-style meals support both children without turning every meal into an event.

risk.rationale: The ground route is credible, but exact 2027 open-jaw flights, the hard June 23 return, automatic-car inventory, Calanques access and bloom timing remain planning gates.

nights.rationale: Twelve hotel nights derives 5/5 under the canonical nights rubric.

novelty.rationale: The Riviera, Cassis, Aix, Verdon and Avignon route is new under the documented visited-place overlap rubric.

pto.rationale: Eight PTO days derives 3/5 and remains unweighted by default; the count becomes nine if the employer does not observe Juneteenth on Friday, June 18.

value.arithmetic: 5,200–6,800 air + 4,200–6,000 lodging + 150–250 Riviera transit + 650–950 car + 350–600 road costs + 1,800–2,600 food + 500–1,000 activities + 500–900 insurance/misc = 13,350–19,100
